title: Disable dev guest login by default (GPE_DEV_LOGIN) — it leaks any account's API key by username
description: POST /api/game/players/guest does find-or-create by username and returns the account's api_key in the body. It is gated only by Settings.dev_login_enabled, which reads GPE_DEV_LOGIN and DEFAULTS TO 'true'. A production deploy that does not explicitly set GPE_DEV_LOGIN=false therefore exposes a route where anyone who knows or guesses a username receives that account's API key — full account takeover with no secret required. The endpoint is rate-limited per-IP (60/hour) but that does not mitigate targeted takeover of a known username, nor distributed enumeration.
impact: Any player's account (and wallet/treasury withdrawal rights, market, mint) can be hijacked by submitting their username. Currency theft and auth bypass; launch-blocking.

evidence.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import os; os.environ.pop('GPE_DEV_LOGIN',None); os.environ['DATABASE_URL']='sqlite:///:memory:'; os.environ['RATELIMIT_ENABLED']='false'; from growpodempire.config import get_settings; get_settings.cache_clear(); from growpodempire.api.flask_api import create_app; app=create_app(); c=app.test_client(); r=c.post('/api/game/players',json={'username':'victim'}); vk=r.get_json()['api_key']; r2=c.post('/api/game/players/guest',json={'username':'victim'}); print('status',r2.status_code,'TAKEOVER',r2.get_json().get('api_key')==vk)"
evidence.output:
dev_login_enabled default = True
victim real key prefix: 2Y3dIDlL
guest status: 200
leaked key prefix: 2Y3dIDlL
TAKEOVER: True

fix.summary: Make dev guest login fail-closed: default GPE_DEV_LOGIN to 'false' so it is OFF unless an operator explicitly opts in for a playtest. Belt-and-suspenders: refuse to enable it when the environment looks like prod (e.g. ALGORAND_NETWORK=mainnet, or a non-sqlite/non-localhost DATABASE_URL), and never return an existing account's api_key — only mint a key for freshly-created guest accounts, or require a per-session token. Add a startup warning log when it is enabled.

test_idea: reports/proposed-tests/test_guest_login_prod_safety.py: assert get_settings().dev_login_enabled is False when GPE_DEV_LOGIN is unset, and POST /players/guest returns 403 by default.
verification_note: Re-ran Dana's command on a fresh app: POST /players/guest returned the victim's EXACT api_key (TAKEOVER=True, 200). Account takeover by username confirmed.

title: Instant harvest exploit: buy->plant->harvest in the same hour yields full top-of-band weight (no grow time), net +923 per cycle
description: harvest_plant() has no growth-stage gate, and the public POST .../harvest route (game_api.py:403-420) forwards straight to it with no extra check. A freshly planted plant has lifetime_hours==0, so Plant.lifetime_vigor falls back to `self.health` (default 100). harvest weight = round(midpoint*(0.4+0.6*vigor/100)) => full top-of-band yield (500g for white-widow) for a plant that never grew. With sell=True the NPC sale posts to the ledger, netting strongly positive. Reachable end-to-end over the live API.
impact: Faucet with no matching sink: a ~25 seed becomes ~+923 balance instantly and repeatably, bypassing the entire grow->care->harvest core loop. Inflation / supply manipulation -> launch blocker.

evidence.output:
start=500.000000 end=1423.648000 net=923.648000 weight=500.0g stage_grew=NO
1 passed in 0.38s

fix.summary: Gate harvest_plant on growth_stage (require FLOWER/HARVEST-ready) and reject if lifetime_hours==0; make lifetime_vigor return a low/zero default (not health) when no hours have accumulated, so an un-grown plant cannot inherit health=100.

test_idea: Assert harvesting a seedling raises GameError (or yields ~floor weight), and that a never-ticked plant cannot net positive.
verification_note: Re-ran Harper's repro (test_harper_instant_harvest_profit.py) — PASS. Same-hour buy→plant→harvest yields full top-of-band weight; ledger net +923/cycle (faucet, no sink).

title: Guest login endpoint is a username/account enumeration + key-disclosure oracle
description: Independent of the default-on gate: even when intentionally enabled for a playtest, guest_login returns the existing account's api_key for any matching username (find-or-create). There is no per-session credential, no proof-of-prior-ownership, and the response is identical whether the account pre-existed. Combined with the 200/key body it doubles as an account-existence oracle and a credential-disclosure primitive. The design comment acknowledges this ('returns an account's API key to anyone who knows the username') but ships it as a returnable production code path.
impact: In any environment where the flag is on (incl. shared staging/playtests), a user can claim other testers' accounts and their in-game funds; also enables username enumeration for the Critical takeover above.

fix.summary: Do not return an existing account's long-lived api_key from guest_login. Either (a) only allow guest login to create brand-new accounts and 409 on collision, or (b) issue a short-lived, rotating session token distinct from the persistent api_key, or (c) require the caller to already present the api_key to 'resume'. Keep find-or-create only for accounts created via guest in the same isolated dev DB.

test_idea: With dev login enabled: create 'alice' via POST /players (capture key A); a different client POSTs /players/guest {username: alice} and must NOT receive key A (expect 403/409 or a session token != A).
cap_notes: kept at severity: conf≥9 self-evident trace
verification_note: Same endpoint as F016 (command-proven key disclosure). find-or-create returns 200+api_key for any username → enumeration + key oracle. Verified via F016's run + code trace.

title: MAX_WITHDRAWAL_PER_DAY cap is bypassable for un-flushed withdrawals in one session
description: _enforce_daily_cap() sums prior ASA_WITHDRAWAL LedgerEntry rows via a query. The session runs autoflush=False (db/session.py:46), and the just-posted withdrawal entry is deliberately not flushed (per the in-code comment). This means ANY prior withdrawal entries that are still pending in the same uncommitted transaction are invisible to the cap query, so multiple withdraw() calls batched in one session bypass the cap. I confirmed with a probe test: cap=150, two withdraw(100) calls in one session_scope — the second one does NOT raise (sum seen = 0, not 100). Across separate committed sessions the cap correctly blocks. The current HTTP route does one withdraw per request (so the request path is presently safe), but the control is latently broken: any future code that calls withdraw() twice in a request, a batch/admin endpoint, or a job loop, silently exceeds the treasury cap. The comment 'isn't double-counted' is the defect, not a feature.
impact: Defense-in-depth treasury cap can be bypassed by any multi-withdraw-per-transaction path; a stolen API key combined with such a path could exceed the daily limit the cap exists to enforce.

evidence.output:
F.
test_two_withdrawals_same_session_should_be_capped: Failed: DID NOT RAISE GameError
(cap=150; withdraw(100) then withdraw(100) in one session — second should be blocked but is not)
test_two_withdrawals_separate_sessions_capped: PASSED
1 failed, 1 passed

fix.summary: Flush the posted withdrawal entry before summing, or include the in-flight amount explicitly, and add a SELECT ... FOR UPDATE / per-player lock so concurrent requests cannot both pass the cap. Compute cap from committed+pending rows: self.session.flush() then query, or sum existing rows AND add the current amount (already added) — the real fix is session.flush() before the query so prior pending entries are counted.

test_idea: reports/proposed-tests/test_blake_withdrawal_cap.py (included): two withdrawals in one session must trip the cap.
verification_note: Re-ran Blake's probe — second same-session withdrawal NOT capped (autoflush=False makes the rolling-sum query miss the unflushed prior row). RECONCILED with Casey F011: the cap IS correct across committed requests; the HTTP route does one-withdraw-per-request, so NOT exploitable today. Real latent defense-in-depth gap + a plausible concurrent-request race. Harden before mainnet.

title: Settlement daily-withdrawal cap (treasury drain defense) is entirely untested
description: _enforce_daily_cap is the rolling-24h per-player treasury limit (defense-in-depth: even with a stolen API key an attacker can't drain more than the cap). tests/test_settlement.py covers only the happy path, linked-wallet, roundtrip, and insufficient-balance cases — coverage term-missing flags settlement_service.py lines 51,62,76-77,103-104,120,126-127, i.e. the cap accumulation/limit branch, the zero-cap disable branch, the negative-amount guard, the chain-failure rollback, and the insufficient-ASA deposit guard. A regression that disabled or mis-summed the cap (it sums -r.amount over ASA_WITHDRAWAL rows) would silently let the treasury be drained with no test catching it.
impact: Payment/treasury path: a broken cap = unbounded on-chain withdrawal per player. Highest-value money-path gap found.

evidence.output:
7 passed in 1.91s
settlement_service.py  68  10  85%  86, 88, 122-135 (was missing 51,62,76-77,103-104,120,126-127 before these tests)

fix.summary: Add reports/proposed-tests/test_casey_settlement_cap.py to the suite: covers single over-cap rejection, accumulation across withdrawals with rollback, cap=0 disable, non-positive guard, chain-failure rollback, insufficient-ASA deposit.

test_idea: Set MAX_WITHDRAWAL_PER_DAY low via a custom Settings, fund a player, assert a single over-cap and an accumulated over-cap withdrawal both raise GameError and (after txn rollback) leave the in-game balance untouched.

title: Pre-migration / never-ticked rows get full-vigor yield via the lifetime_vigor health fallback
description: Migration c1d2e3f4a5b6 backfills lifetime_health_sum/lifetime_hours with server_default '0'. Any plant created before the migration (or any plant never advanced by catch_up under the new accumulator) has lifetime_hours==0, so lifetime_vigor returns self.health instead of an integrated average. A mature, full-health legacy plant therefore harvests at full top-of-band weight regardless of how it was actually grown -- defeating the whole 'lifetime care sets yield' design.
impact: Legacy/un-migrated plants ignore the new lifetime-vigor mechanic and pay max yield; an exploiter can also keep a plant at lifetime_hours==0 to dodge the integrator.

evidence.output:
legacy fallback weight=500.0 vigor=100.0 hours_after_harvest=0.0
1 passed

fix.summary: When lifetime_hours==0 at harvest, treat vigor as a conservative default (e.g. seed/baseline, not current health). Optionally backfill lifetime_health_sum from a sane proxy at migration time, or block harvest until at least one simulated hour has accrued.

test_idea: A plant with lifetime_hours==0 and health=100 must NOT harvest at top-of-band weight.
verification_note: Re-ran Harper's edge test — pre-migration/never-ticked row (lifetime_hours==0) harvests at FULL vigor via the health=100 fallback, defeating the new lifetime-care mechanic for legacy rows.

title: plant_dict serializes lifetime_vigor but Plant TS interface omits it (serializer↔client drift)
description: serialize.plant_dict() emits `lifetime_vigor` (round(plant.lifetime_vigor,1)) on EVERY plant payload (list, single, and /state). The hand-written client `Plant` interface in web/src/lib/types.ts (lines 117-133) does NOT declare a `lifetime_vigor` field. Verified by an AST/regex diff of serializer keys vs TS interface fields: the only Plant drift is exactly `lifetime_vigor`. lifetime_vigor is the headline new mechanic — it is the integrated average health that sizes harvest weight (game_service.py:799 `vigor = max(0.0, min(100.0, plant.lifetime_vigor))` → weight_g = midpoint * (0.4 + 0.6*vigor/100)). The web client cannot type-safely surface the value that determines a player's yield. No test guards serializer↔TS parity (test_openapi.py only checks paths/security, not body schemas; the TS file header itself states 'OpenAPI spec carries no body schemas').
impact: Client UI cannot expose or reason about lifetime vigor (the field that drives harvest weight) without an untyped escape hatch; future renames of the field on either side go undetected. Bounded: additive field, no balance misreport, existing consumers unaffected.

evidence.output:
serialize.py lifetime_vigor count: 1
web/src/lib/types.ts lifetime_vigor count: 0
AST diff: Plant: in serializer but NOT in TS -> ['lifetime_vigor']
serialize.py:106:        "lifetime_vigor": round(plant.lifetime_vigor, 1),
game_service.py:799: vigor = max(0.0, min(100.0, plant.lifetime_vigor))  # drives harvest weight

fix.summary: Add `lifetime_vigor: number;` to the Plant interface in web/src/lib/types.ts (after `health`), mirroring serialize.plant_dict.

title: Chamber canvas is fully inert under prefers-reduced-motion, but UI still tells users to swipe to brush
description: createPlantRenderer captures motionOK once at construction (line 303-305). The pointer listeners (pointerdown/move/up/cancel) AND the rAF loop are wired ONLY inside `if (motionOK)` (856-866). So when a user has prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the chamber detail page still renders the hint 'Swipe across the plant to brush the branches' (page.tsx:81) but the canvas registers zero pointer listeners and never drives physics — brushing does nothing. A single static frame is drawn via draw(0). The instructional copy is desynced from actual behavior.
impact: Reduced-motion users (an accessibility-sensitive cohort) see an interaction prompt that silently does nothing. Not a leak — destroy() is safe — but a fragile gating decision: a11y preference disables an unrelated input affordance. Also motionOK is read once, so toggling the OS setting mid-session won't re-wire.

fix.summary: Decouple input wiring from motion preference: always attach pointer listeners (brushing is discrete, not motion), and gate only the continuous sway/wind animation on motionOK. Run a minimal rAF (or render-on-interaction) loop so physics + dust respond even in reduced-motion. Alternatively hide the 'swipe' hint when !motionOK.

test_idea: jsdom/RTL test: mock matchMedia to return matches:true for reduced-motion, mount PlantCanvas mode='chamber', dispatch a pointerdown+pointermove on the canvas, assert a handler ran (e.g. spy on canvas.addEventListener count > 0) — currently 0.
verification_note: Not re-run this shift (severity ≤ Medium; outside the Critical+top-High audit worklist). Agent evidence stands as reported.

title: Mock and real providers diverge on transfer source — mock cannot surface the deposit duplication bug
description: MockChainProvider.transfer_asset ignores sender_mnemonic entirely and ALWAYS debits TREASURY, crediting the receiver. AlgorandProvider honors sender_mnemonic (defaulting to treasury) and resolves receiver==TREASURY to the treasury address. So for deposit() (receiver=TREASURY, no sender), the mock debits TREASURY and credits TREASURY (book net unchanged) while the real provider does a treasury self-transfer that never touches the player's wallet. Because the mock has no per-player external-wallet book, the deposit duplication (finding #1) is structurally invisible to CI. This is provider parity drift: the mock does not faithfully model who-is-debited, so the one place the abstraction matters most for settlement correctness is untested.
impact: CI green gives false confidence; settlement correctness bugs that depend on real sender/debit semantics cannot be caught with the current mock.

evidence.output:
56 def transfer_asset(self, asset_id, receiver, amount, sender_mnemonic=None):
59   book = self.balances.setdefault(asset_id, {})
60   book[TREASURY] = book.get(TREASURY, 0) - amount   # always debits TREASURY, ignores sender
61   book[receiver] = book.get(receiver, 0) + amount

fix.summary: Make the mock honor sender (default treasury) and keep a per-address book so a player->treasury vs treasury->player transfer is distinguishable; then deposit() against the mock will reveal that the player's ASA is not being reclaimed.

test_idea: Mock transfer with an explicit player sender must debit that player's book, not TREASURY; deposit() must reduce the player's mock-wallet ASA.
verification_note: Not re-run this shift (severity ≤ Medium; outside the Critical+top-High audit worklist). Agent evidence stands as reported.

title: Toast region is not a live region — error/success toasts are silent to screen readers (covers money/auth failures)
description: The toast container is a plain <div> with no aria-live/role. Toasts are the ONLY surfaced feedback for auth and money actions: quick-play/login failures ('Quick play is disabled', 'That API key doesn't match this Player ID', 'Sign in failed'), account creation, and harvest/sell results all route through toast.error/success. A screen-reader or voice-control user gets no announcement that their sign-in or sale failed; the message appears, auto-dismisses after 4s, and is never read. This blocks completing/diagnosing money & auth actions non-visually, which is why it rates above the usual low a11y band.
impact: Blind/low-vision users cannot tell a money/auth action failed or succeeded; they may retry a guest login or a sell repeatedly with no feedback.

title: Compute-on-read catch-up is O(hours) single-threaded; ~410ms per idle-year per plant on one read
description: catch_up() advances a plant in fixed 1-hour Python steps from last_tick_at to now. A plant read after a year idle runs the full 8760-iteration loop synchronously inside the request. Measured 411ms for 365 days (8760 steps) and 39.8ms for 30 days on this box (in-memory SQLite). The loop mutates the ORM object every hour: cProfile shows ~294k SQLAlchemy attribute __get__ + ~74k attribute set calls dominating (~0.27s of 0.66s tottime), plus per-hour compute_conditions() and a fresh sha256-seeded RNG. Cost scales linearly with idle hours and is paid on the read path (GET /plants/<id>/state -> SimulationService.sync). Each living plant card polls /state every 7s (usePlantState POLL_MS=7000), so the expensive case is the cold first read after a long idle, not steady-state polling.
impact: A player returning after weeks/months pays a multi-hundred-ms CPU stall per plant on first load; with a 7s poll fanned out per card across a populated garden, several plants can cold-sync near-simultaneously and saturate a worker. Not launch-blocking at expected scale but a real latency/CPU regression worth bounding (batch, or precompute closed-form for long gaps).

evidence.command: PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -c '<bench: setup white-widow plant, catch_up over N days, time.perf_counter>'
evidence.output:
days=  30 hours=   720 catch_up_time=    39.8ms events=7 alive=True
days= 365 hours=  8760 catch_up_time=   411.0ms events=9 alive=True
CAP   hours=8760  catch_up_time=   409.6ms events=9 alive=True
# cProfile tottime: engine._step 0.137 (8760 calls); sqlalchemy attributes.__get__ 0.116 (294206 calls); attributes.set 0.096 (73834); _health_target 0.094; Random.seed 0.063; compute_conditions 0.050 (8761)

fix.summary: For large gaps, vectorize/precompute the deterministic decay+health drift in plain floats and only touch the ORM object once at the end (events still emitted at stage boundaries). Or run catch-up off the request path (background sweep) and serve last-synced state on read. Keep the 1hr fidelity only for the recent window.

test_idea: Benchmark/assert catch_up(8760h) completes under a target (e.g. <100ms) and that a long-idle read yields identical plant state to the iterative loop (golden-state regression).
verification_note: Spot-check: max_catchup_hours clamp confirmed at engine.py:255; a plant idle beyond the cap advances only cap hours/read and never fully catches up. Mechanism verified.

title: deposit() never reclaims the player's on-chain ASA — withdraw+deposit duplicates real tokens
description: deposit() calls provider.transfer_asset(asset_id, TREASURY, units) with no sender_mnemonic. In AlgorandProvider.transfer_asset, sender_mnemonic=None makes the SENDER the treasury and receiver==TREASURY resolves to the treasury address, so the on-chain transaction is treasury->treasury (a no-op). Per algosdk semantics the SENDER's holding is what gets debited, so the player's GROW ASA (which was really transferred to their external wallet during withdraw()) is NEVER pulled back. Yet deposit() still credits the player full in-game GROW via post(ASA_DEPOSIT). The DB-side wallet.asa_balance counter only limits the deposit to what was withdrawn, but the actual on-chain ASA stays in the player's wallet. Net effect on the real chain: withdraw 100 (player gets 100 real ASA) -> deposit 100 (in-game GROW restored, player KEEPS the 100 ASA) -> repeat. The player accumulates real tradeable ASA for free while keeping in-game balance whole = value duplication / treasury drain. The Mock provider hides this because it has no model of the player's external wallet and debits TREASURY in both directions.
impact: On mainnet/TestNet a linked player can mint unlimited real GROW ASA out of the treasury by looping withdraw->deposit, draining the treasury asset supply. Mock-only CI cannot catch it.

evidence.output:
settlement_service.py:123 self.provider.transfer_asset(self.asset_id, TREASURY, self._base_units(amount))  # no sender_mnemonic
algorand.py:86 sk = mnemonic.to_private_key(sender_mnemonic) if sender_mnemonic else self.treasury_sk
algorand.py:96 if receiver == TREASURY: receiver = self.treasury_addr
-> sender=treasury, receiver=treasury: self-transfer, player ASA never debited.

fix.summary: deposit() must pull the ASA FROM the player's address. Either require a signed player->treasury axfer (game must verify the inbound txid via the indexer before crediting), or treat deposit as off-chain only and never run a provider transfer. Crediting in-game GROW must be gated on a confirmed on-chain receipt of the player's ASA into the treasury, not on a treasury self-transfer.

test_idea: Real-provider (or a mock that tracks a separate player wallet book) test: after withdraw(100) the player wallet holds 100 ASA; deposit(100) must leave the player wallet at 0 ASA and treasury restored. Today the player wallet stays at 100.
verification_note: Code-trace CONFIRMED: deposit() calls provider.transfer_asset(asset_id, TREASURY, units) with no player-signed inbound transfer — a custodial server cannot pull a user's ASA as written, so the DB debits while the real asset never moves. Exact on-chain effect needs TestNet → unverifiable here. Real pre-mainnet design gap; add to the mainnet checklist.

title: NFT mint is not idempotent across a chain-success / DB-rollback boundary — duplicate on-chain assets
description: _mint() sets status PENDING, calls provider.create_asset() (irreversible on-chain), then sets nft_asset_id + MINTED. Idempotency in mint_harvest/mint_strain only short-circuits when nft_status==MINTED. If create_asset() succeeds but the surrounding session_scope commit fails (DB error, conflict, crash between create_asset and commit), the on-chain ASA exists but the row is rolled back to its prior status (none/failed) with no asset id. A retry calls create_asset() AGAIN and mints a SECOND on-chain NFT for the same harvest/strain. There is no reconciliation by metadata_hash or url, and no persistence of the asset id before the chain call, so the only durable link (nft_asset_id) is lost on rollback. FAILED rows are intentionally re-mintable, which compounds this.
impact: Supply/uniqueness violation: a single eligible harvest/strain can back multiple on-chain NFTs, breaking the 1:1 collectible guarantee and enabling duplicate-NFT sale/trade.

evidence.output:
110 def _mint(self, row, asset_name, url, metadata):
111   row.nft_status = NFTStatus.PENDING.value
112   self.session.flush()
113   try:
114     asset_id = self.provider.create_asset(... )   # irreversible on-chain
122   except ChainError: row.nft_status = FAILED; raise
126   row.nft_asset_id = asset_id
127   row.nft_status = NFTStatus.MINTED.value   # lost if outer commit fails -> retry re-mints

fix.summary: Persist a mint-intent (deterministic external key, e.g. harvest_id) and check the chain for an existing asset before create_asset, or record nft_asset_id+txid in a committed step before returning success. At minimum, treat PENDING as 'verify on-chain before re-minting' rather than re-minting unconditionally, and key create_asset off an idempotency token so a retry is a no-op.

test_idea: Simulate create_asset success then force a commit failure; on retry, assert create_asset is not called a second time / no duplicate asset id is created.
verification_note: Not re-run this shift (severity ≤ Medium; outside the Critical+top-High audit worklist). Agent evidence stands as reported.

title: Linked Algorand address is not unique and not validated — multiple players can share an address

Two or more players can link the same address; withdraw() then sends treasury ASA to a shared/attacker-controlled address. There is no proof the linking player controls the address, so an attacker can link a victim's known address (or a shared exchange address) and have withdrawals routed there.

fix.summary: Validate the address via algosdk.encoding.is_valid_address, add a uniqueness constraint (or explicit policy if sharing is intended), and require a signed-message challenge proving the player controls the private key before allowing withdrawals to it.

title: Withdrawal daily-cap check is TOCTOU-racey under concurrent requests
description: withdraw() posts the debit, then _enforce_daily_cap() sums prior ASA_WITHDRAWAL entries created in the last 24h to decide if the cap is exceeded. With autoflush off, the just-posted entry isn't counted (by design), and there is no row lock or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the player's wallet/ledger. Two concurrent withdraw requests for the same player can each read the same 'already withdrawn' total, each pass the cap check, and both commit — letting total withdrawals exceed the configured 24h cap. The wallet.version bump is not used for optimistic-lock enforcement here. Impact is bounded (overshoot ~= one extra request's worth per race window) but it weakens the treasury control.
impact: A scripted attacker with a valid/stolen key can modestly exceed the per-day treasury cap by issuing parallel withdrawals; the harder the cap is relied on as the sole brake, the worse this is.

evidence.output:
entry = post(self.session, player_id, -amount, LedgerEntryType.ASA_WITHDRAWAL, ...)
        # Then enforce the rolling-24h treasury cap. The just-posted entry isn't
        # flushed yet (autoflush is off), so it isn't double-counted; ...
        self._enforce_daily_cap(player_id, amount)
        # no row lock / SELECT FOR UPDATE -> concurrent txns read stale 'already' sum

fix.summary: Serialize per-player withdrawals: take a SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the wallet row (or use the wallet.version optimistic lock with a retry) before computing the 24h sum, so concurrent withdrawals are ordered and the cap holds. On Postgres, an explicit row lock on Wallet at the top of withdraw() is sufficient.

test_idea: Simulate two interleaved withdraw() calls in separate sessions against the same player with a cap that allows only one; assert exactly one succeeds.
verification_note: Not re-run this shift (severity ≤ Medium; outside the Critical+top-High audit worklist). Agent evidence stands as reported.

title: max_catchup_hours cap defers, not discards: a multi-year-idle plant needs one ~400ms read per capped year to fully catch up
description: elapsed_hours is clamped to max_catchup_hours (8760), but the loop only advances plant.last_tick_at by the iterations it actually runs. So a plant idle 3 years processes 8760h on the first read (advancing last_tick_at by exactly 1 year) and is still 730 days behind; full catch-up requires 3 sequential ~400ms reads. The cap therefore bounds a single read's cost but NOT the total work to become current, and for auto-water/auto-feed pods (which keep the plant alive so the death break never fires) every one of those reads pays the full 8760-iteration cost. The cap is sane as a single-read DoS guard but its semantics (work deferred across reads, not collapsed) are easy to misread.
impact: An auto-pod plant left idle for years stays perpetually behind unless polled repeatedly, each poll costing ~400ms; a script hammering /state on such a plant extracts ~400ms CPU per request. Bounded per-request, but unbounded in aggregate and surprising.

evidence.command: PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -c '<auto_water+auto_feed plant, idle 3yr, single catch_up read, measure advance>'
evidence.output: 1st read of 3yr-idle: 382.2ms, advanced 8760h (1.00yr), alive=True, still_behind=730d

fix.summary: Either (a) on a gap larger than the cap, snap last_tick_at = now after one capped pass (accept the documented fidelity loss) so a plant can't stay behind, or (b) close-form the skipped hours. Document the cap's deferral semantics either way.

test_idea: Assert that after one catch_up of an N>cap-hour idle plant, (now - last_tick_at) is either ~0 (snap) or exactly N-cap hours, and that a hostile loop of reads has bounded total cost.
verification_note: Spot-check: max_catchup_hours clamp confirmed at engine.py:255; a plant idle beyond the cap advances only cap hours/read and never fully catches up. Mechanism verified.

title: One rAF loop + ResizeObserver per PlantCanvas; dashboard mounts N independent renderers with no visibility gating
description: createPlantRenderer() starts its own requestAnimationFrame loop, its own ResizeObserver, and (chamber mode) its own pointer listeners per canvas. PlantCard renders exactly one PlantCanvas per plant, and PodCard/dashboard map PlantCard over every plant in every pod (pod/PodCard.tsx line 61-62, dashboard/page.tsx line 98-99) with no IntersectionObserver/virtualization. So M pods x P plants = M*P concurrent rAF loops. Each frame (throttled to ~30fps via the 33ms gate at plantRenderer.ts:790, but rAF itself still fires ~60Hz per card) clearRects and redraws a full procedural plant: a 24-segment spine, up to 13 nodes each with a flower site of multiple clusters x (bracts+2) pods + hairs + trichomes, plus the apical cola. buildPlant() is rebuilt whenever the key (stage|round(health)|indicaRatio|symptom|alive|seed|mode|WxH) changes, and ResizeObserver fires buildPlant directly on every resize with no debounce.
impact: On a populated garden (e.g. 16 plants) this is 16 always-on animation loops compositing fairly heavy 2D canvas work every frame, even for off-screen cards. Noticeable battery/CPU and jank on low-end mobile. Bundle size is fine (renderer is dependency-free; dashboard route 6.76kB / 137kB First Load JS).

evidence.command: cd web && npm run build  (and grep PlantCanvas/PlantCard usage)
evidence.output:
Route (app)                         Size  First Load JS
/dashboard                       6.76 kB         137 kB
/dashboard/plants/[plantId]      3.21 kB         137 kB
+ First Load JS shared by all             102 kB
# PlantCard.tsx:64 renders <PlantCanvas .../> ; PodCard.tsx:61 plantIds.map(id=><PlantCard.../>) ; dashboard/page.tsx:98 orphanLocal.map(...). plantRenderer.ts:853 new ResizeObserver(resize); :864 raf=requestAnimationFrame(frame) -- per instance.

fix.summary: Pause off-screen renderers with a shared IntersectionObserver (stop rAF when not visible), and/or drive all canvases from one shared rAF ticker. Debounce ResizeObserver->buildPlant. Reduced-motion already short-circuits rAF (motionOK gate) -- good.

title: Breed accepts any strain ids: no ownership/discovery gate and no self-cross guard

title: Renderer rebuild key omits wall-clock grow day, so a live plant never ripens between stage/health changes
description: deriveDay() (125-135) derives the displayed grow day from Date.now() - plantedAt. But frame() only rebuilds geometry (buildPlant) when `key` changes (794-798), and key is composed of stage|health|indicaRatio|symptom|alive|seed|mode|WxH — it does NOT include the elapsed day. plantedAt is stable per plant, so for a plant whose stage/health are unchanged between 7s polls, budDev/ripe/brown/trich (all functions of the day) stay frozen at the value captured on the last rebuild.
impact: Mostly cosmetic: visible ripening only advances when the polled health/stage changes (which they usually do during active grows), so it self-corrects in practice. But on a stable-health flowering plant the buds visually stall. Low because the sim is server-authoritative and health/stage churn masks it.

// deriveDay (125-135) uses Date.now(); day is not in key, so devParams(d) is frozen until another field changes

fix.summary: Include a coarse day bucket in the rebuild key, e.g. append `|${Math.floor(deriveDay(p.stage, p.plantedAt))}` so geometry rebuilds at least once per grow-day even when health/stage are steady.

The companion StatBars expose numbers elsewhere, but the canvas itself (often the focal element on a card) is uninformative.

title: PlantCanvas writes propsRef.current during render (render-phase side effect)
description: propsRef.current is assigned in the component body (65-74), i.e. during render, not in an effect. The ref-funnel pattern is intentional and works here (the renderer reads getProps() each frame, so it always sees the latest committed value), and it is not stale. But mutating a ref during render is technically a render-phase side effect that React's docs advise against; under React 18 StrictMode/concurrent double-render or a bailed-out render the timing is benign here only because the rAF read happens post-commit.
impact: Low: no observed bug — the value the renderer reads is always the most recent assignment, and there is exactly one renderer instance. Flagged as a fragile-pattern note, not a defect. Confidence capped (trace-only, no failing command).

fix.summary: Optional: move the propsRef assignment into a useEffect (or useLayoutEffect) keyed on the inputs to keep render pure. Behavior is unchanged; this only satisfies the 'do not write refs during render' guidance.

test_idea: N/A behavioral; lint rule react-hooks could be augmented but no functional test warranted.
verification_note: Not re-run this shift (severity ≤ Medium; outside the Critical+top-High audit worklist). Agent evidence stands as reported.

title: require_player distinguishes 404 (no such player) from 403 (bad key), enabling player-id enumeration
description: require_player returns 404 'Player not found' when the player_id doesn't exist and 403 'Invalid API key' when it does but the key is wrong. The differing status/message lets an unauthenticated caller enumerate valid player_ids (UUIDs, so practically hard to brute, but the oracle still exists and pairs with the guest-login username oracle). The hmac.compare_digest comparison itself is correct/constant-time; the leak is the branch before it.
impact: Player-id existence disclosure; low on its own (UUID space) but compounds enumeration when combined with the guest endpoint.

fix.summary: Return a uniform 401/403 with a generic message for both 'no such player' and 'bad key' on write/owner-scoped routes, so the response does not reveal whether a player_id exists. Keep the constant-time compare.

test_idea: Assert that GET/POST on a non-existent player_id and on an existing player_id with a wrong key return the same status code and body.
verification_note: Not re-run this shift (severity ≤ Medium; outside the Critical+top-High audit worklist). Agent evidence stands as reported.

title: set_environment syncs every plant in a pod in a Python loop; cost stacks with catch-up amplification
description: set_environment() queries all living plants in a pod and calls self.sync(plant) (engine.catch_up) for each in a Python for-loop so they catch up under the old environment before new readings apply. This is correct, but if multiple plants in a pod are long-idle, the per-plant catch-up cost (up to ~400ms/idle-year, see engine finding) multiplies by the plant count within a single write request. The query itself is fine (one filtered .all(), no N+1), but the per-row catch_up makes one set_environment call potentially capacity*400ms.
impact: A single environment update on a full pod of long-idle plants could take capacity x several-hundred ms. Minor at expected idle gaps but compounds the engine catch-up cost; worth noting alongside it.

evidence.output:
src/growpodempire/services/simulation_service.py:207-213
        plants = (
            self.session.query(Plant)
            .filter(Plant.pod_id == pod_id, Plant.harvested.is_(False), Plant.is_alive.is_(True))
            .all()
        )
        for plant in plants:
            self.sync(plant)

fix.summary: Same remedy as the engine finding -- a cheaper long-gap catch-up makes this loop cheap. No N+1 query issue; the cost is purely the per-plant simulation work.

test_idea: Time set_environment on a pod of capacity N long-idle plants; assert it scales acceptably after catch-up optimization.
verification_note: Spot-check: max_catchup_hours clamp confirmed at engine.py:255; a plant idle beyond the cap advances only cap hours/read and never fully catches up. Mechanism verified.

title: compute_conditions() runs every catch-up hour, doubling the per-step work for onset-event diffing
description: Inside the per-hour catch_up loop, compute_conditions(plant, sim) is called every iteration (8761 calls for a year) purely to diff condition onsets and emit condition_onset events. cProfile shows compute_conditions at ~0.05s tottime over a year plus the surrounding set/get churn. Condition transitions are rare relative to hours; recomputing the full flag set every hour is wasted work in the common case where nothing changes.
impact: A constant multiplier on the already-linear catch-up cost. Small in isolation but part of why an idle-year read is ~400ms rather than tens of ms.

evidence.output:
8761    0.050    0.000    0.110    0.000 .../simulation/reactions.py:14(compute_conditions)
# called once per hour inside the loop (engine.py:269) plus once at the end (engine.py:282)

fix.summary: Only recompute conditions when a driving level crosses a threshold (cheap guard on water/nutrient/pest/disease deltas), or compute onsets from the state trajectory in bulk for large gaps rather than per-hour.

test_idea: Assert identical emitted condition_onset events before/after the optimization across a representative trajectory (golden test).
verification_note: Spot-check: max_catchup_hours clamp confirmed at engine.py:255; a plant idle beyond the cap advances only cap hours/read and never fully catches up. Mechanism verified.
